question.worked_solution:
To find $\lambda ,$ we want to match the expression

$$
c=\frac{4}{3}a+\lambda b.
$$

We are given that one of the components is $\frac{4}{3}a.$ So, we first draw the vector $\frac{4}{3}a$ from the origin. Then we complete the path to the point $C.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14251995/assets/b8db5015e22e55282e180b1d81f7a2e1ca544dfe0f468dc4dedb6283bac2da5c.png)

Let $P$ be the endpoint of the vector $\frac{4}{3}a.$ Then

$$
c=\overset{\to }{OP}+\overset{\to }{PC}.
$$

In $△OPC,$ we have:

- $PC=\frac{1}{4}|b|$

- $\overset{\to }{PC}$ and $b$ have the same direction

Hence, $\overset{\to }{PC}=\frac{1}{4}b.$

Additionally,

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =\overset{\to }{OP}+\overset{\to }{PC} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}a+\frac{1}{4}b.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $c=\frac{4}{3}a+\lambda b=\frac{4}{3}a+\frac{1}{4}b.$

Since $a∦b,$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. Equating the coefficients of $b,$ we get:

$$
\lambda =\frac{1}{4}.
$$
